clothing-store.definition: A store where customers purchase clothes and other items they wear.

shoe-store.definition: A retail shop that sells footwear to customers.

electronics-store.definition: A shop that sells electronic devices, appliances, and related accessories.
electronics-store.exampleUsage: The electronics store displays phones and headphones.

bookstore.definition: A shop where books are sold.

toy-store.definition: A shop that sells toys and games.
toy-store.exampleUsage: The toy store has puzzles near the entrance.

jewelry-store.definition: A shop that sells jewelry such as rings, necklaces, and bracelets.

sports-store.definition: A shop that sells sports clothing, footwear, and equipment.
sports-store.exampleUsage: The sports store sells balls, rackets, and training gear.

pet-store.definition: A shop that sells pet food, supplies, and sometimes live companion animals.
pet-store.exampleUsage: The pet store sells food and carriers for cats and dogs.

pharmacy.definition: A shop or service where medicines are dispensed and health products are sold.

department-store.definition: A large shop sells many kinds of products, with each group displayed in a different section.

escalator.definition: Moving stairs that carry people between floors.

elevator.definition: A machine that carries people or goods up and down between floors.
elevator.exampleUsage: The elevator was used during the activity.

fountain.definition: A structure that sends water upward and lets it fall back down.

directory.definition: A map or list showing the mall's shops and facilities.

bench.definition: A long seat for several people.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.

parking-garage.definition: A building or covered structure with multiple spaces for parking vehicles.
parking-garage.exampleUsage: The mall parking garage has several levels.

entrance.definition: Something that provides access (to get in or get out).

exit.definition: A doorway or route used to leave the building.

security-office.definition: An office used by security staff to monitor and manage safety at a property.
security-office.exampleUsage: A lost item was taken to the security office.

food-court.definition: An area, often in a shopping mall, where several fast-food outlets surround a shared dining space.

tray.definition: An open receptacle for holding or displaying or serving articles or food.

table.definition: A flat-topped piece of furniture used to display goods or eat at.

fast-food.definition: Food prepared and served quickly, often for takeaway.

drink-station.definition: A self-service or staffed area where drinks are dispensed or collected.
drink-station.exampleUsage: The food court has a drink station beside the tables.

menu-board.definition: A displayed list of available food, drinks, prices, or options.
menu-board.exampleUsage: The menu board showed the meal choices.

line.definition: A queue of people waiting for their turn.

high-chair.definition: A tall chair with a tray or safety features for seating a small child at table height.
high-chair.exampleUsage: The restaurant provided a high chair for the toddler.

shopping-bag.definition: A bag made from plastic or durable paper, often with handles, carries purchased goods home from a shop.

wallet.definition: A pocket-size case for holding papers and paper money.

credit-card.definition: A payment card that lets you borrow money for purchases and repay it later.

receipt.definition: A written or digital record showing that a payment was made.

sale-sign.definition: A sign announcing that products are being sold at reduced prices or under a promotion.
sale-sign.exampleUsage: A sale sign was displayed in the shop window.

mannequin.definition: A model of the human body used to display clothing.

fitting-room.definition: A private room where customers can try on clothes before deciding whether to buy them.
fitting-room.exampleUsage: She tried the jacket in the fitting room.

size-tag.definition: A label on clothing or footwear that shows its size.
size-tag.exampleUsage: The size tag was sewn into the collar.

price-tag.definition: A label showing how much an item costs.

cinema.definition: A place where people watch films on a large screen.

arcade.definition: A building filled with electronic games and machines.
arcade.exampleUsage: The arcade was used during the activity.

bowling-alley.definition: A place with long lanes where people play bowling.
bowling-alley.exampleUsage: The mall has a bowling alley on the upper floor.

play-area.definition: A designated space for children’s games and other leisure activities, usually outdoors but sometimes indoors, that provides equipment or is simply reserved for play.

carousel.definition: A ride with decorated seats that moves slowly around a centre.

photo-booth.definition: A small enclosed space where people take photographs.

karaoke.definition: Singing popular songs accompanied by a recording of an orchestra (usually in bars or nightclubs).

trampoline-park.definition: An indoor recreation facility with connected trampolines and padded activity areas.
trampoline-park.exampleUsage: The trampoline park requires visitors to follow posted safety rules.

mini-golf.definition: A recreational putting game played on a small course with short themed holes and obstacles.
mini-golf.exampleUsage: The family played mini golf at the entertainment center.

climbing-wall.definition: An artificial wall with holds designed for supervised climbing practice.
climbing-wall.exampleUsage: The climbing wall has safety equipment and trained staff.

shopper.definition: A person who visits shops to buy things.

security-guard.definition: A person who protects a building and its people.

janitor.definition: A person who cleans and maintains a building.

cashier.definition: A worker who takes payments and gives change or receipts.

sales-clerk.definition: A shop employee who helps customers and handles sales or merchandise.
sales-clerk.exampleUsage: The sales clerk checked whether another size was available.

information-desk.definition: A staffed service point helps visitors in public or institutional buildings find their way, ask questions, and obtain general assistance.

gift-wrapping.definition: The service or activity of covering a present in decorative paper or packaging.
gift-wrapping.exampleUsage: The mall offers gift wrapping during the holiday season.

delivery-pickup.definition: A designated place or service for collecting an order that was purchased or arranged for delivery.
delivery-pickup.exampleUsage: The customer collected the parcel at the delivery-pickup counter.

lost-and-found.definition: A service that stores lost belongings so their owners can claim them.

stroller.definition: A small wheeled chair used to transport a baby or young child.
